todaysEvents.summary: Trump vows to declare Hormuz US territory
todaysEvents.delta: Trump said he'll declare the Strait a 'territory of the United States' after Iran is 'defeated'; Iran's Deputy FM Gharibabadi rejected the claim, vowing to keep enforcing the blockade (Al Jazeera, Aug 14).

todaysEvents.summary: UAE says Iran struck two ADNOC tankers
todaysEvents.delta: UAE blamed Iran for drone strikes on two ADNOC-affiliated tankers transiting Hormuz Thursday, calling it 'piracy'; 15 ADNOC vessels hit since the war began (Al Jazeera, Aug 14).

todaysEvents.summary: Iran, Oman 'homing in' on strait deal
todaysEvents.delta: Bloomberg reported Iran and Oman are nearing a Hormuz strait-management arrangement even as ship attacks mount, building on their Aug 8 route-coordinate agreement (Bloomberg, Aug 15).

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Iran and the US move toward a workable framework normalising Hormuz transit; Iran and Oman are reportedly 'homing in' on a strait-management arrangement (Bloomberg, Aug 15), but Trump's claim he will declare the strait 'US territory' and Iran's firm rejection (Al Jazeera, Aug 14) show no near-term signed reopening. Brent moves toward $75-85 as the risk premium eases, while Qatar's force majeure still limits LNG availability.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: No workable full-reopening agreement emerges: fresh drone strikes hit two ADNOC-affiliated tankers (Al Jazeera, Aug 14) even as Iran-Oman route talks progress (Bloomberg, Aug 15); Iran still ties reopening to US compliance with the June MoU, an end to Israeli strikes on Lebanon, unfrozen assets and reparations. Brent holds $78-95 and JKM stays elevated on Qatar force majeure through mid-September.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Trump's pledge to declare Hormuz 'US territory' and Iran's vow that the strait will be 'closed or opened solely under Iran's authority' (Al Jazeera, Aug 14) raise the risk of renewed full closure and spillover into the Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb, especially if fresh tanker attacks continue. Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu as Gulf cargoes become inaccessible.
